data.cultural_impact: The name Devshanthan holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, representing the highest power and authority. It is a revered name that signifies dignity, leadership, and divine protection. In Hindu mythology, Devshanthan is sometimes depicted as a powerful deity, often depicted carrying a trident or holding a conch shell, signifying the creation and destruction of the universe. This name is echoed in various forms of Hindu art, literature, and rituals.
data.spiritual_significance: Devshanthan is a deeply spiritual name that reminds us of the ultimate divine authority. It signifies the connection between the individual soul and the cosmic consciousness, emphasizing devotion, reverence, and surrender to the divine force. Serving as a reminder of the fundamental unity of all existence, the name Devshanthan inspires spiritual growth and a deeper understanding of the shared divine source of all beings.

historical_references.reference: Devshanthan was a revered Hindu sage and a disciple of sage Narada. He is also known as Vedavyas, as he was the one who organized and codified the Vedas in the form of the four Vedas - Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda. The process of codification is said to have taken place during the early Vedic period around 1500 BCE.

Devshanthan is also revered in the Shaiva tradition as the first human to worship Lord Shiva. The story goes that Devshanthan did severe penance and was blessed by Shiva with the vision of the God. This event is said to have taken place during the Shiva Purana era, around 500 CE.
historical_references.context: First human to worship Lord Shiva
